scope: public-data restricted-six-taxon descendant-lineage sensitivity; not primary event-origin T3 after Japanese-core chronology refinement

dated_scaffold.chronology_refinement: Public Japanese core Nipponocirsium are nodding and split from the Taiwan core at ~0.74 Ma. Cross-study reconciliation therefore moves the parsimonious U->D transition deeper, after the ~0.79 Ma C. morii split and before the ~0.74 Ma Japanese-Taiwan core split. Because these node ages come from separate dated analyses with overlapping marginal intervals, 0.74-0.79 Ma is a central-age sensitivity, not a joint posterior branch interval.
dated_scaffold.consequence: Taiwan 0.79-0.47 Ma palaeoclimate is retained as a descendant-lineage/restricted-tree sensitivity and must not be described as the unique environment of orientation origin.

decision.interpretation: Within the restricted Taiwan descendant-lineage sensitivity, no exceptional annual-precipitation or precipitation-seasonality variability is detected. This result cannot be promoted to the actual orientation-origin environment after public Japanese core Nipponocirsium shift the parsimonious transition deeper and render the transition paleolocation unresolved.

claim_boundary: Do not generalize this restricted-tree result to the actual U->D origin, all 4-6 Japan38 changes, historical rainfall causation, adaptation or convergence.
